sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro preview — Gemini API model documentation
sources.evidence: The exact standard preview ID has a 1,048,576-token input limit, text/image/video/audio/PDF inputs, text output, thinking and function calling. The customtools endpoint is separately identified. Documentation updated October 9, 2026. Reopened October 27, 2026: the exact endpoint specifications supply no total or active parameter count.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro — Google Cloud model documentation
sources.evidence: Google Cloud lists the standard preview on February 19, 2026 and its customtools endpoint on February 23. The Gemini API changelog records both endpoints on February 19; the later Cloud date does not establish the earliest customtools release. Confirms standard-model context and capabilities.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro — Model Card
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The exact card explicitly names Gemini 3 Pro as the model dependency and architecture/training-data reference. This is a valid named-base relationship, but neither its model information nor its complete comparison tables gives a numerical total or active count.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Pro Model Card (updated May 2026)
sources.evidence: Rechecked the complete May 2026 card freshly retrieved October 27. Page 2 explicitly lists Gemini 3.1 Pro as a dependent model; page 3 describes sparse MoE routing. The named base has no published numerical total, active count, expert dimensions or routing width here. Gemini 3 Pro itself is explicitly not a modification or fine-tune of an earlier model.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: The service terms linked from the exact model card govern API access and prohibit extraction or replication of underlying models and parameter weights, supporting proprietary distribution rather than an open-weight license.

sources.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash — Model Card (May 2026)
sources.evidence: Later first-party comparison card includes an exact Gemini 3.1 Pro column for capabilities, but contains no total/active parameter disclosure for it. Flash specifications are not transferred. Fresh full-card and exact-model comparison-table check October 27, 2026 reconfirmed no numerical total or activated-parameter column.

sources.title: Gemini 3.6 Flash — Model Card (July 2026)
sources.evidence: Later first-party comparison table includes Gemini 3.1 Pro, without total or active parameter counts. Its benchmark and price entries do not establish model size. Fresh full-card and exact-model comparison-table check October 27, 2026 reconfirmed no numerical total or activated-parameter column.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon — Model Card (October 2026)
sources.evidence: Later successor card compares safety results against Gemini 3.1 Pro, without disclosing its total or active parameter counts. Argon is explicitly a new model, so its specifications are not transferred. Fresh full-card and exact-model comparison-table check October 27, 2026 reconfirmed no numerical total or activated-parameter column.

sources.title: SFT Drives Gemini’s Safety Properties
sources.publisher: Google DeepMind Language Model Interpretability team (Josh Engels, Arthur Conmy, Bilal Chughtai and Neel Nanda)
sources.evidence: June 13, 2026 author research update explicitly studies pretraining-only, SFT and production Gemini 3.1 Pro. The training/interpretability study adds no numeric model size or architecture detail. Reopened October 27: the post identifies pretraining/SFT/production stages but no count-bearing checkpoint or numerical size.

sources.title: Models.dev Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview record
sources.evidence: Original catalog source inspected as a lead. Its name and endpoint identify this standard preview; technical values were checked independently against Google documentation.

sources.title: Gemini API release notes — February 19, 2026
sources.evidence: The February 19, 2026 entry explicitly launches gemini-3.1-pro-preview-customtools alongside Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Safety & Security Report
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27 full-text review of the complete report and Gemini 3.1 Pro comparisons found no retrospective size disclosure. Parameter mentions concern evaluation difficulty, weight security and encoded knowledge, not a numeric total or active model count.

sources.title: What LLMs Must Forget to Teach Effectively: A DIY Approach to Premodern Japanese Language Pedagogy, v1
sources.publisher: Stilerman et al., independent application research
sources.evidence: Opened October 27 to inspect a concrete numerical lead. The conclusion asserts more than two trillion parameters for Gemini 3.1 Pro without a supporting developer citation. This is not accepted nominal size evidence.

sources.title: What LLMs Must Forget to Teach Effectively: A DIY Approach to Premodern Japanese Language Pedagogy, v2
sources.publisher: Stilerman et al., independent application research
sources.evidence: Opened the revised version October 27. The earlier more-than-two-trillion assertion is absent. The application paper provides no verified total or active count for the model.

sources.title: Google (Gemini) — GPT-5.6 Pro deep dive, Frontier Inference Margins
sources.publisher: Frontier Inference Margins, independent scenario analysis
sources.evidence: Opened October 27 after an active-count search. The page explicitly marks its 3T total midpoint and 120B active assumption as speculation for economic sensitivity analysis, says actual counts are unknown, and describes the artifact as model-generated analysis. Neither number is a developer disclosure or measured size.

sources.title: Incompressible Knowledge Probes: Estimating Black-Box LLM Parameter Counts via Factual Capacity, v2
sources.publisher: Bojie Li / Pine AI, independent research
sources.evidence: Opened October 27 to examine the numeric-estimation lead. The method estimates open-model-equivalent factual capacity from black-box responses with roughly threefold uncertainty in either direction, rather than reporting Google nominal counts. Table 2 explicitly excludes Gemini 3.x because Gemini 3.1 Pro was a calibration landmark and the Flash lineage inherits its inflation; the study supplies no accepted total or active specification for this preview.

name.note: Official endpoint title and model ID identify the standard preview.

developer.note: Google DeepMind publishes and develops the model; Google is the catalog developer label.

family.note: Catalog normalization of the documented Gemini 3 Pro family and 3.1 Pro dependency.

release_date.note: The standard preview launched February 19 in both the Gemini API changelog and Cloud versions table.

open_weights.note: Official distribution is through Google services/API under proprietary terms, without a downloadable open checkpoint.

license.note: Descriptive model-access classification under Gemini service terms; documentation and sample-code licenses are separate.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-name/ID total-size and named-base searches, reopened original evidence and later Google comparisons found no supported nominal total. The exact card explicitly names Gemini 3 Pro, but that base also has no published numerical count. The uncited greater-than-2T assertion was removed in a revised application paper; scenario and black-box capacity estimates are not substituted. Null reflects absent count evidence, not an exact tensor-census requirement.

active_parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 active/activated-count searches and later exact-model comparison tables found no numerical per-token active count for this preview or its named Pro base. Sparse routing is explicit, but expert dimensions and routing width are not. The 120B serving-cost assumption is explicitly speculative; no active count is inferred from total-capacity estimates or benchmarks.

architecture.note: Exact card explicitly delegates architecture to Gemini 3 Pro: sparse mixture-of-experts Transformer, not an unsupported family inference.

context_window.note: Exact API input-token limit; separate output cap is 65,536 tokens.

modalities.note: Exact endpoint supports these input formats and text output; no image or audio generation.

tool_call.note: Function calling is explicitly supported by the standard endpoint.

summary: Fresh parameter re-audit October 27, 2026: total and active counts remain explicitly null after exact-model searches, original card/API and named-base checks, later Google comparison cards, training research and the Gemini 4 safety report. Investigated an uncited greater-than-2T assertion removed in a later paper version, speculative 3T/120B serving scenarios and independent black-box capacity estimates. None establishes a nominal count. All unrelated field assessments and corrections are preserved.
